text:
devin: quick question — thinking about adding a "grace window" in the fallback UX. idea: operator can set 0-30s window where we prefer to keep trying primary model before degrading. what do ppl think?

maria: 👍 makes sense. need to make it explicit it's about latency vs error thresholds

sam: can we default to 5s and expose a tooltip that says "prefers primary for this duration"? also want a test button in console to simulate spike

devin: agree. also thinking different modes: soft (return cached + partial), quiet (return shorter response), hard (immediate fallback). names bikeshed welcome

olivia: +1 on mode names, maybe call them: grace, partial, failfast — easier to explain in runbooks

ops-bot: deploy-check: rollout flag "fallback_grace_experiment" enabled for 20% of orgs

maria: telemetry ask: record: trigger_reason, final_mode, latency_at_trigger, tokens_saved, sample_of_original_output (for audit). sampling rate configurable

sam: on audit retention, let's store sampled traces 90d by default, with a UI to replay. also need RBAC so only SRE/product can view raw outputs

devin: UX question: should console show an inline "why we fell back" pill next to each request with brief reason + link to trace? I think yes

olivia: yep. also add quick CTA "compare with primary" that runs side-by-side diff in the trace viewer

maria: small API change: include fallback_meta in response headers when fallback happened: {mode, trigger, sampled_trace_id}

sam: sample curl for new header:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
      https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
      -d '{"prompt":"test"}' \
      -i

# response headers show: X-Redwood-Fallback: mode=grace;trigger=latency;trace=abc123

devin: perfect. last q: default sampling rate? ops-bot suggests 0.1% org-wide, 5% for orgs in experiment

ops-bot: enacted: sampling_rate=0.1% / experiment=5% (logs will show sample_tag)

maria: followups: write runbook snippet + console tooltip copy. I'll PR copy this afternoon

devin: thanks all. will sketch the UI and link in a mock next

olivia: 😄
